_meta.raising_a_ceiling: Shrinking always passes. Raising one means the boot payload grew: justify it in the commit body, and never do it to make a red gate green. RAISED AT v1.173.1, gzip only, 385,000 -> 386,400 (+0.36%), and the arithmetic is the whole justification. MEASURED IN CI (the deploy's own gate, run 33775959154): 385,900 against 385,000 — 216 curated journeys passed and this byte count was the single failure. WHERE THE BYTES WENT, measured by building the SAME source tree at three refs and gzipping neural.js: v1.170.1 153,550 -> dev's v1.172.0 154,176 (+626, dev's own two ships) -> this merge 156,105 (+1,929, the three bottom layers). So the ceiling had ~1,000 of headroom and the feature needed ~1,900: dev spent part of it before this branch merged. WHAT WAS TRIED FIRST, because 'never do it to make a red gate green' is the rule above: two duplication sites were consolidated — one ghost-button factory for the four layer handles, and one check-row builder shared by the questions toggle and the three layer rows — which measured 288 bytes, and the settings rows in FULL are only 438, so no amount of tidying reaches 900. Closing the gap would mean deleting a handle the owner asked for by name (the hand ✕, whose crowding is why the see-more hint was removed in this same ship). Those two refactors are NOT in this commit: the disk was full and the box could not run Playwright, so the code here is byte-for-byte the tree CI validated, and only this number moved. WHAT THE BYTES BUY: the film row, the question card and the hand each collapse from their own handle and stay collapsed across landings, reloads and devices — the owner's 'it should still be collapsed'. THIS IS THE OWNER'S CALL TO REVISIT: the ceilings are targets from Cloudflare Observatory field data (LCP P75 13,764ms), and 1,400 bytes gzip is 0.36% of the first-hand payload. If they would rather stay under 385,000, the 288-byte trim plus dropping the three settings rows (438) gets most of the way and only the hand ✕ would still have to go. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.175.1, gzip only, 386,400 -> 387,400 (+0.26%), same shape of justification and the same owner's call. MEASURED IN CI (the deploy's own gate, run 33806320372): 386,753 against 386,400 — 217 curated journeys passed and this byte count was the single failure, so the deploy step was skipped and the dev preview went stale. WHERE THESE BYTES WENT, measured by building the SAME tree at two refs and gzipping neural.js (-9): dev at 37db2595b 155,498 -> the corridor keyboard 156,079, i.e. +581 gzip / +2,143 raw for the Challenges corridor's keyboard (v1.175.0). The remaining ~270 of the 853 since the last CI measurement are dev's own two ships in between (#206 labels, #207 Last-rolls repaint) — nobody spent it twice. WHY IT COULD NOT BE PAID FOR BY SHEDDING: the feature IS 581 gzip and the overage was 353, so closing it meant deleting more than half of what the owner asked for by name (↑/↓ walking the ladder, or ⏎ grading). The cheap trims were measured first and are not enough: the ⏎ chip on Got-it and the focus try/catch together are ~290 raw / ~120 gzip. The three boot JSONs were checked for whitespace waste in the same pass and are already minified (raw == json.dumps with separators, all three). THE GATE'S AUTHORITY IS THE DEPLOY BUILD: it is the only one that carries the injected PostHog snippet (/postscript.js 78,095 B there vs 75,641 keyless), ~2,450 raw the PR's e2e-full never sees — so this ceiling must be read off a deploy run, never off a local or PR build, or the headroom is a fiction. 387,400 leaves ~650. THIS IS THE OWNER'S CALL TO REVISIT: if the answer is 'stay under the target', the keyboard's ↑/↓ is the piece to cut, and it should be cut deliberately rather than by a byte count.
